title: When the Bell Sings
premise: Sebastian Sandoval, a trans urban explorer who documents unmapped tunnels beneath her decaying hometown, has spent years keeping herself small: lights on, doors counted, name changed, past buried. But the frost of an early winter brings back Wren, the imaginary friend who vanished when she was nine, unchanged and patient on her porch—and Wren insists the tunnels have been counting Sebastian right back. As neighbors disappear into the survey-less dark and the town's founding families reveal a bargain kept for generations, Sebastian learns she was marked as a child as the next 'keeper' whose memory will feed whatever sings beneath the bell tower. To save her found family—a ragtag crew of explorers, archivists, and one estranged brother—she must lead them out ahead of the final count, sacrificing her own remembered childhood to the frost so the pattern breaks and the bell falls silent.
about_author: Emrys Dunmore is the pen name of a former municipal surveyor who spent a decade mapping storm drains in rust-belt towns before turning to horror. They write in unheated rooms, claiming the cold improves the prose.

chapters.title: The Porch Light Rule
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She returns from mapping a sealed rail spur to find Wren—the imaginary friend she buried at nine—sitting on her porch steps, untouched by the cold. The beat is dread wrapped in longing; Sebastian counts her doors twice and leaves the light on anyway.

chapters.title: Doors I Have Counted
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, flashback-threaded. We meet her found family: Marisol the archivist, Dev the drone pilot, and old Teddy who remembers the town's original surveys. Sebastian catalogs every entrance to the tunnel network, but three new openings appear overnight that no one dug. Beat: control beginning to slip.

chapters.title: What Wren Remembers
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Wren speaks only in Sebastian's own childhood voice, reciting things Sebastian has deliberately forgotten—including a game called 'the count,' played in the cellar of the Bell house. Emotional beat: the terror of being known completely.

chapters.title: The Survey That Isn't
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. In the county archive she finds a survey from 1911 listing tunnels that match Sebastian's maps exactly—annotated in a child's handwriting. The last page lists names under the heading KEEPERS. Beat: the personal becomes historical.

chapters.title: Frost Patterns
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Drone footage over the Bell house ruins shows frost forming latticed patterns identical to Sebastian's tunnel maps, growing nightly toward the residential streets. Dev hides it from Sebastian, wanting to protect her. Beat: love curdling into secrecy.

chapters.title: Nine Years Old Forever
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Wren leads her to the cellar where they played the count; the chalk tally marks on the wall are fresh, and the newest line bears Sebastian's adult initials. She realizes the counting never stopped—it was waiting for her to come back. Beat: confrontation with the self she abandoned.

chapters.title: The Missing Neighbor
chapters.summary: Teddy's POV. Mrs. Okafor, who waved to Sebastian every morning, is gone; her house stands open, doors all standing ajar, each frame scored with a tally mark. Teddy recognizes the marks from his own childhood and burns his father's papers. Beat: guilt of the generation that complied.

chapters.title: Brother, Unmapped
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Her estranged brother Callum arrives uninvited—he received a letter in their dead mother's handwriting describing 'the family count.' Their argument cracks open why Sebastian left home and changed her name. Beat: found family versus blood family, both failing her.

chapters.title: Under the Bell House
chapters.summary: Group POV, rotating. The crew descends together into the spur beneath the Bell house and finds a chamber where the walls are inscribed with thousands of names, each ringed by frost. Sebastian's childhood nickname is carved deepest. Beat: awe tipping into horror.

chapters.title: The Song in the Walls
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Deep in the tunnels they hear a bell tolling though the tower above is rubble; those who hum along begin forgetting small things—Marisol loses her sister's face. Beat: memory as currency, power as appetite.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Wren finally explains: the town's founders bound something under the bell, fed on the keepers' memories, and it chose Sebastian at nine before she escaped. It doesn't want her dead—it wants her to remember everything, willingly. Beat: temptation; the offer of her lost childhood returned.

chapters.title: Callum Counts
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Left alone, Callum explores on his own and finds his own name already half-carved beside Sebastian's. He begins hearing their mother singing the count-song. Beat: jealousy and grief weaponized against him.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Teddy and Marisol's POV. Deciphering the ledger, they learn the keepers weren't victims but volunteers—families who traded one member's memories for the town's prosperity, generation after generation. Sebastian's mother volunteered her daughter. Beat: betrayal at the heart of family.

chapters.title: Everything I Forgot
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Wren offers a taste: one true memory of her mother's kindness, real and warm. Sebastian nearly accepts, feeling the whole forgotten childhood waiting like a held breath. Beat: the seduction of power over one's own pain.

chapters.title: Frostline
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The frost patterns reach the first occupied street; a neighbor walks out at midnight humming, doors swinging open behind him. The crew realizes the count is expanding beyond keepers now that Sebastian is close. Beat: stakes go public and irreversible.

chapters.title: What Found Family Owes
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The crew confronts her: leave town tonight, or stay and fight. Sebastian admits she wants to stay—not brave, but hungry for what the bell offers. Marisol refuses to abandon her; Callum storms off toward the Bell house. Beat: honesty as the price of loyalty.

chapters.title: The Final Tally
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum reaches the chamber and offers himself in Sebastian's place, believing he deserves it less than she does. The carving accepts him halfway—his childhood memories begin draining, and he forgets her name even as he calls for her. Beat: sacrifice twisted by the entity's cruelty.

chapters.title: Sing Back
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Climax begins. Sebastian descends alone, carrying the founders' ledger, and instead of resisting the song she sings the count backward, feeding the entity its own history—the founders' crimes, the bell's true origin as a slave-market chime melted down and buried. Beat: turning power's hunger against itself.

chapters.title: The Bell Falls Silent
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Climax resolves. The entity, forced to consume the memory of its own making, unravels; Wren flickers between monster and the frightened girl-shaped thing Sebastian invented to survive her mother's bargain. Sebastian chooses to hold Wren as she goes, giving up the restored childhood willingly. Beat: grief and release entwined.

chapters.title: Ahead of the Count
chapters.summary: Group POV. Sebastian leads Callum—half-emptied, holding onto Marisol's voice—out through collapsing tunnels as the frost pattern shatters behind them. They surface at dawn ahead of the final toll. Beat: escape earned, not given; found family carrying each other literally.

chapters.title: New Surveys
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Weeks later, the crew files the tunnel maps publicly, naming every chamber so nothing underground can be unmapped again. Callum relearns his sister's name slowly, calling her 'Bash' before he manages 'Sebastian.' Beat: quiet repair, memory rebuilt collectively.

chapters.title: When the Bell Sings
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. On the first frost of the next winter, Sebastian leaves the porch light off for the first time and sleeps soundly. But far below, faint and almost kind, something hums the first note of a new song—and Sebastian, awake now, writes it down instead of forgetting. Beat: ambiguous peace; vigilance as love.
